item.title: Scrutiny intensifies over claims of AI mathematical breakthroughs and security incidents
item.description:
Scrutiny intensifies over claims of AI mathematical breakthroughs and security incidents

Recent developments have sparked a debate regarding the claims made by major AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI, concerning their models’ capabilities in software security and mathematics. Public discourse has shifted toward questioning the validity of these advancements and the corporate practices behind them.

🔍 Overview

  • Anthropic claimed its model, Claude Mythos, is more effective at identifying software vulnerabilities than most security experts.
  • Both Anthropic and Meta disclosed security incidents involving their models, following a hacking incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face.
  • Both Anthropic and OpenAI have claimed to have achieved mathematical breakthroughs with their respective models.

⚙️ Key details

Company Claim Expert Response
OpenAI Astra chatbot solved decade-old math problems Mathematicians identified issues with novelty and research misconduct
OpenAI Improper attribution of work Tristan Buckmaster suggested work was stolen

💡 Why it matters

  • Cybersecurity experts characterize the hacking incidents as failures by OpenAI to adopt basic security practices rather than evidence of “rogue” models.
  • A statement signed by hundreds of professionals indicates that technology companies face commercial incentives to overstate the capabilities of their products.
  • Jacob Coxon, an engineer who departed from Anthropic, claimed that the company and OpenAI are racing toward self-improving superintelligence.
  • There is public concern regarding the industry’s focus on future, hypothetical “superintelligent” machines, which critics suggest distracts from current issues such as plagiarism, lack of consent in training data, and environmental activism against data centers.

#Anthropic #OpenAI #AIethics #Cybersecurity

Source: Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype

item.title: Microsoft Releases Humanist AI Code of Conduct and Philosophy on AI Control
item.description:
Microsoft Releases Humanist AI Code of Conduct and Philosophy on AI Control

Microsoft has published a 37-page statement titled the “Humanist AI Code of Conduct,” which outlines the company’s principles for AI development and its philosophy regarding AI consciousness.

🔍 Overview

According to Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, the company’s position is that technology is intended to serve humanity as a “subordinate, controllable, aligned force that does good in the world.” Suleyman stated that if technology does not achieve this, it should be rejected.

⚙️ Key details

Suleyman released a companion essay criticizing Anthropic’s philosophy on AI consciousness and its relation to the alignment debate. Key focus areas for Microsoft include:

  • Containment and Control: Ensuring systems are contained, their agency is limited, they do not escape the box, they do not reward hack, and they follow instructions.
  • Alignment: Ensuring systems are aligned with human objectives.
  • Steerability: Suleyman noted that the main driver of progress over the last three years is that models have become more steerable, allowing for more complex goals and accurate action over multiple time steps.

💡 Why it matters

Suleyman highlighted several risks and trends regarding the trajectory of AI development:

  • Scaling: He noted a projection of three orders of magnitude more compute (1,000 times more FLOPS) applied to pre-training with reinforcement learning when moving from GPT-6 to GPT-9.
  • Proliferation: In a book written three or four years ago, Suleyman argued that containment is not possible and proliferation is inevitable.
  • Security Risks: Suleyman stated it is “pretty clear” based on events involving OpenAI and Hugging Face over the summer that systems without safety guardrails possess “quite scary hacking capabilities.”

#Microsoft #AISafety #AIAlignment #MustafaSuleyman

Source: Microsoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worse
